Migrated lane state: RED at closure install, before any build. `npm install --no-audit --no-fund` under consent VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10 / VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=consented failed with npm ERESOLVE; no tarball was fetched, so there is no acquired URL or digest to record. First conflict: @ant-design/icons-angular@13.1.0 peers @angular/common@^13.0.1 against the aligned root ^16.2.0.

Cut line: the adapter's cell aligns @angular/*, @angular-devkit/*, @schematics/*, @ngrx/*, @angular-eslint/* and the karma/jasmine toolchain. It says nothing about the Angular-major-coupled COMMUNITY library layer this application has and factoriolab did not: ng-zorro-antd 13, @ant-design/icons-angular 13, @datorama/akita 7 with akita-ng-entity-service / akita-ng-router-store / akita-ngdevtools, @ngneat/{content-loader,until-destroy,tailwind}, @sentry/angular 6, ngx-quill 16, @storybook/angular 6 plus four addons, and codelyzer 6 / nz-tslint-rules (a TSLint line with no Angular 16 release at all). Each declares a peer range on the Angular major, so every era copy refuses the target line.

Decision needed before a retry: should the cell gain an `ecosystemPackages` table (same generic shape as the existing `testPackages`, keyed by package name, applied to any manifest) naming the version each community library publishes for the target Angular major? That is generic in form, but populating it honestly needs registry-verified versions per package, and the codelyzer/nz-tslint-rules pair has no Angular 16 successor at all — dropping them is a decision about the application's lint cell, not a mechanical rewrite.

Scope warning for the re-cut: this is very likely NOT a config-only hop. ng-zorro 13->16, Akita's Angular bindings, and @ngneat/until-destroy 8->v10+ carry API changes, so applicationFilesChanged will probably move off 0 and may need one or more new source transforms. I would cut it as: (a) one unit to declare and evidence the ecosystem table and get the closure to resolve, (b) one unit for the migrated build plus whatever source transforms the compiler then demands, (c) build-level parity. Attempting all three in one unit is what ran this one past its budget.

summary: Verified the jira-clone journey in the browser on both lanes and measured every fact the cell needs (seven style probes identical across lanes, exact seam inventory, drag/modal/create/filter selectors, scroll absence, seed-board restore). Three spec contradictions surfaced: create-issue is navbar item :nth-of-type(3) (item 2 is a search drawer whose overlay hangs the journey), one Backspace does not widen the filter, and the reload cancels a third Sentry envelope POST whose failure the generic inventory would record by full URL including the DSN public key. Wrote no repository files; the remaining work also exceeds one unit.
open_questions: The reload aborts an in-flight Sentry envelope POST (net::ERR_ABORTED) even with the 200 application/json {} answer. The generic tallyFailedRequests records non-loopback failures by full URL including the sentry_key query, leaking the DSN, and the count is load-timing dependent so it cannot be pinned exactly. Authorise one of: (a) a generic AppSpec redactFailedRequestPath hook so the pinned entry carries no query, (b) admitting it through the corroborated cancelled-duplicate-fetch category (two 200 siblings of the same method/path exist in-run), or (c) dropping the reload, which would also drop the after-online-reload zero-service-worker checkpoint.

Journey (d): typing 'Witness' narrows the board to 1/0/0/0, but a single Backspace leaves it narrowed because 'Witnes' still matches. Confirm the widening gesture: clear the field entirely (select-all + Backspace), click the app's own 'Clear all' control, or assert narrowing only.

Re-cut needed: the remaining work is the AppSpec plus four journeys, renderedStyles wiring through executeRun and runReactBaselineDifferentialProfile, a ~700-line core schema, the runner, and two test files. Split into (1) core schema plus real-app-run wiring and (2) journey plus runner plus tests.
